title: Check your accounts for charges you did not make

cards.text: The CFPB says to check your accounts often. Open paper statements and review them, or check transactions online.
cards.line: A short check can catch a problem early.

cards.text: The CFPB says to contact your bank or card provider at once if you suspect an unknown charge. Use the number on your card or statement.
cards.line: Call as soon as something looks wrong.

cards.text: The CFPB says to keep copies of your letters and write down the dates of your follow-up calls. Keep it all together in a file.
cards.line: Keep the details close when you call.

checks.prompt: How often should you look at your account activity?
options: Only when a bill is late
checks.why: The CFPB says to check often and read statements closely.

checks.prompt: You see a charge you did not make. What should you do?
options: Ask a friend to check it
checks.why: The CFPB says to contact your bank at once if you see an unknown charge.

checks.prompt: You called your bank about an unknown charge. What next?
options: Keep a record of your calls
checks.answer: Keep a record of your calls
checks.why: The CFPB says to keep copies of your letters and write down the dates you call.

takeaway: Check often, save details, and contact your bank quickly about unknown charges.

sources.name: CFPB, Watch accounts closely when card data is hacked
